## Week by week

Each week's page collects that week's lecture notes, slides, lab notebook, and presentation papers in one table. Every week's topic and papers are listed from the start; the materials for a week are released in the week it is taught.

| Wk | Topic | Lecture | Lab |
|---|---|---|---|
| [1](week01.qmd) | Course intro · What is an agent? | agent = control flow decided by model output; components; autonomy | first API calls · prompting fundamentals |
| [2](week02.qmd) | Prompting & reasoning | chain-of-thought · self-consistency · test-time compute | CoT & exemplars, measured on a math evalset |
| [3](week03.qmd) | Tool use | function calling · tool schemas · the capability boundary · code execution | functions into tools (Ng M3) |
| [4](week04.qmd) | The agent loop (ReAct) | loop anatomy · Act-only vs ReAct · the internalized protocol · trace reading | the loop built by hand |
| [5](week05.qmd) | Reflection & evaluation | Self-Refine · Reflexion · evalsets · LLM-as-judge · error analysis | reflection, measured against an evalset (Ng M2+M4) |
| [6](week06.qmd) | Multi-agent systems | division-of-labor patterns · handoffs · context isolation · MCP | multi-agent pipeline (Ng M5) |
| [7](week07.qmd) | Planning & search | decomposition · plan–execute–replan · ReWOO · ToT | research-agent workflow (Ng final project) |
| [8](week08.qmd) | **Midterm exam** | written, W1–7 | — |
| [9](week09.qmd) | Retrieval augmentation (RAG) | embeddings · pipeline · agentic RAG | retriever for the final project |
| [10](week10.qmd) | Context engineering · Memory | Lost in the Middle · select/order/compress · MemGPT · Mem0 | memory · graph integration |
| [11](week11.qmd) | Reasoning models & RL | o1/R1 · STaR · RLVR · GRPO | thinking-budget measurement |
| [12](week12.qmd) | Inference economics · Benchmarks | cost–accuracy trade · routing · Pareto · pass^k | routing + cost logging · eval harness |
| [13](week13.qmd) | Safety & security · Retrospective | indirect prompt injection · defense layers | guardrails · red team |
| [14](week14.qmd) | **Final presentations** | team demos + eval scorecard defense | — |
| [15](week15.qmd) | **Final exam** | written, whole semester | — |

Ordering principle: concept dependency — every week is understandable using only what came before it. Materials appear on each week's page as the semester progresses.

## The course in one sentence

You will learn how LLM agents work by **building one, week by week**, and by reading the papers that invented each part. The final deliverable is a research-assistant agent that searches and synthesizes answers over this course's own paper corpus.

## Weekly rhythm (3 hours)

| Block | Time |
|---|---|
| Theory lecture | 30–40 min |
| Paper presentations ×2 | 50 min |
| Break | 10 min |
| Lab (Colab notebook) | 80 min |
| Wrap-up · next-week preview | 10 min |

Labs run in Google Colab through `aisuite` with your own API key — no local installation. Each week page offers its notebook as a `.ipynb` download; upload that file to [Colab](https://colab.research.google.com) yourself (**File → Upload notebook**) and run it there. From Week 3 most labs adapt Andrew Ng's *Agentic AI* (DeepLearning.AI) nearly as given (the Week 4 loop lab is course-built); Weeks 1–2 practice prompting, and every week from Week 2 adds a small graded homework.

## Before the first class

1. Read the [API Setup Guide](api-setup.qmd) and issue your own API key. The Week 1 lab needs it in class.
2. Bring a laptop that can open [Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com) in a browser.
